issue: Does an improper denial of a defendant's Faretta right to self-representation automatically render a later voluntary guilty plea involuntary, so that the plea voids the claim?

sides.position: An improper denial of the right to self-representation renders any subsequent guilty plea per se involuntary and voids the plea.
cases: United States v. Hernandez, 203 F.3d 614, 626 (9th Cir. 2000)

sides.position: An improper denial of the right to self-representation does not render a subsequent guilty plea involuntary, so the guilty plea waives appellate review of the denial.
cases: United States v. Moussaoui, 591 F.3d 263, 279–80 (4th Cir. 2010)
United States v. Dewberry, 936 F.3d 803, 805–07 (8th Cir. 2019)
United States v. Montgomery, 529 F.2d 1404, 1407 (10th Cir. 1976)

quote: As we are barred by Williams's forfeiture from addressing the circuit split on the question of whether an improper denial of a defendant's Faretta right to self-representation automatically renders a guilty plea involuntary, we make no comment on the decisions of our sister circuits.
cite: United States v. Elbert Lee Williams, 29 F.4th 1306 (11th Cir. 2022)
